beats.text: What if your database outgrows one machine?
beats.say: What happens when your database grows too big for a single machine?

beats.text: One machine = one limit. Bigger ones get very expensive.
beats.say: One database has a limit on storage and on traffic, and bigger machines get expensive, fast.

beats.text: Sharding splits the data across many databases.
beats.say: Sharding splits the data across several databases, called shards. Each shard holds only a part of it.

beats.text: The shard key picks the shard: user ID % 3.
beats.say: A shard key decides where each row lives. For example, user I D, modulo three.

beats.text: A bad shard key creates a hot shard.
beats.say: But a bad shard key creates a hot shard, where one server gets most of the traffic.

beats.text: Cross-shard queries are slow. Choose your key carefully.
beats.say: Queries that span shards get slower, and resharding later is painful. So choose your key carefully.
